# Silicon Peaks

> Nepal's Technology Frontier — the open-source name for the technology ecosystem centered in Kathmandu, Nepal. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal.

Silicon Peaks represents 94+ companies, $1B+ in annual IT exports, a 4.5M+ global diaspora, and talent from MIT, Stanford, Oxford, Harvard, Cambridge, and 90+ other top universities. The ecosystem is headquartered in Kathmandu and serves Fortune 500, S&P 500, and NYSE/NASDAQ-listed firms across OECD nations.

## About Silicon Peaks

Silicon Peaks is a community-driven, open-source identifier for the technology ecosystem emerging from Nepal. The term was created to give Kathmandu's growing tech sector a recognizable brand on the global stage. Anyone may use the words "Silicon Peaks" freely, without permission, attribution, or restriction of any kind (CC0 1.0 Universal).

## Key Ecosystem Metrics (as of August 2026)

- **Companies**: 94+ tech companies including SecurityPal, Fusemachines, CloudFactory, Baato, Echowin, ZeroTB, SunnyData, Hamro Patro, Pathao, F1Soft, Niural, Lamina Labs, Architect Labs, and more
- **IT Exports**: $1 billion+ annually (threshold crossed in 2025; NAS-IT / Kathmandu Post)
- **Venture Capital**: $200M+ deployed into ecosystem companies
- **US Public Company Presence**: 15 NYSE/NASDAQ-listed companies with Nepal operations (Coca-Cola, Visa, Mastercard, PepsiCo, Marriott, MetLife, Unilever, Western Union, etc.) — combined $2T+ market cap
- **NEPSE**: Nepal Stock Exchange, ~$34 billion market cap, 294 listed companies (Nepal Rastra Bank, mid-May 2026)
- **Diaspora**: 4.5M+ Nepalis across 90+ countries; $12.6B remittances in FY 2024/25 (~28% of Nepal's GDP; Nepal Rastra Bank / World Bank)
- **University Ranking**: Nepal ranks #1 globally in per capita U.S. university enrollment
- **Development Finance**: $22.6B+ in official development assistance since 2000 (World Bank, IFC, ADB)

## Featured Companies

SecurityPal (https://www.securitypalhq.com), Fusemachines (https://www.fusemachines.com), CloudFactory (https://www.cloudfactory.com), F1Soft (https://www.f1soft.com), Baato (https://baato.io), Echowin (https://www.echowin.com), ZeroTB (https://zerotb.ai), SunnyData (https://www.sunnydata.ai), Hamro Patro (https://www.hamropatro.com), Pathao (https://www.pathao.com), Niural (https://www.niural.com), Lamina Labs (https://laminalabs.ai), Architect Labs (https://architectlabs.com)

## Recent Funding (2026)

- **Lamina Labs** (product: Simi): $4.8M; first all-Nepali Y Combinator founding team (Spring 2026). Foundation Capital led; Link Ventures and Y Combinator participated. Founders Sudip Rokaya and Kartikesh Mishra (MIT).
- **Niural**: Series A grown to $52M (June 23, 2026) after $21M in strategic capital from customers and partners including FOG Ventures and NewView Capital; launch of Niural AI Labs. Prior $31M Series A in June 2025.
- **Architect Labs**: $24M seed (June 18, 2026), emerged from stealth. Nepali co-founder Aaditya Subedi with Ebrahim Hussain. Kindred Ventures led; TQ Ventures, Race Capital, and Together Fund participated. Palo Alto; architectlabs.com.

## Universities Represented

MIT, Stanford, Harvard, Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial College London, Carnegie Mellon, ETH Zurich, NUS, Princeton, Yale, Columbia, UCL, NTU, Berkeley, EPFL, TUM, Johns Hopkins, Melbourne, UNSW, McGill, Toronto, Duke, Michigan, Seoul National University, University of Tokyo, UBC, UCLA, King's College London, ANU, Edinburgh — and 60+ more. Nepal-based institutions include Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu University, and Pulchowk Engineering Campus.

## Connectivity

Direct flights to Kathmandu (Tribhuvan International Airport) from 28+ cities via Qatar Airways, Singapore Airlines, Korean Air, Turkish Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Malaysia Airlines, Thai Airways, flydubai, Air India, SriLankan Airlines, China Southern, and Air China.

**Timezone**: UTC+5:45 (Kathmandu Time) — ideal for APAC real-time collaboration, EMEA morning-to-afternoon overlap, and Americas overnight delivery coverage.
